description: Taxonomy to describe how information was collected during open-source intelligence (OSINT) investigations. The 'osint' taxonomy describes the type of source; this taxonomy describes the specific collection technique or tradecraft used to gather the information, so that other analysts can understand how a piece of intelligence was obtained, assess its reliability and reproduce the collection.

predicates.description: Techniques using search engines to discover content or metadata exposed on the public web.
Techniques to extract information from images and videos.
Techniques to collect information from social media platforms and online communities.
Techniques to collect information from domain name, DNS and network infrastructure records.
Techniques to retrieve past or removed content from archives and historical records.
Techniques to collect information from official public records and registries.
Techniques to collect information from satellite imagery, mapping and movement tracking data.
Techniques to collect information from leaked or breached datasets.

entry.description: Advanced search queries (dorks) combining operators and site or filetype filters to find exposed content, files or login pages.
Retrieving cached copies of web pages from search engine caches when the live page changed or was removed.
Finding documents through metadata indexed by search engines (author, creation software, embedded GPS in documents).
Automated monitoring of new search results via alerting services such as Google Alerts.
Uploading an image to reverse image search engines (e.g. TinEye, Google Lens, Yandex) to find earlier, original or related versions.
Determining where a photo or video frame was taken by matching landmarks, infrastructure and terrain against maps and imagery.
Determining when an image or video was captured using shadows, sun position, weather or seasonal cues.
Extracting metadata embedded in image files (GPS coordinates, camera model, timestamp, editing software).
Analysing a public profile: posts, photos, biography, behaviour and declared affiliations.
Pivoting from one account to related accounts through friends, followers, groups, mentions and interactions.
Passively monitoring a platform from a controlled sock puppet account; engaging with human subjects crosses into HUMINT and requires OPSEC and proper authorization.
Collecting posts, profiles or metadata through official or third-party APIs of social media platforms.
Recovering deleted posts, comments or profiles from web archives, caches or third-party mirrors.
Historical DNS resolution data collected passively from passive DNS providers, without querying the target.
Historical WHOIS registration records of a domain (registrar, registrant changes, name servers).
Subdomain and certificate data published in public Certificate Transparency logs.
Reverse DNS or reverse IP lookup to find other hostnames or domains hosted on the same infrastructure.
Searching internet-wide scanning databases (e.g. Shodan, Censys) for exposed services, banners and certificates.
Enumerating subdomains of a domain via CT logs, search engines, DNS records and public datasets.
Retrieving archived copies of web pages from web archives (e.g. Wayback Machine, archive.today, national web archives).
Searching paste sites and their archives for previously published text, credentials or dumps.
Examining the commit history of public code repositories to find removed code, secrets or deleted files.
Consulting official company registries: registration, officers, shareholders, filings and addresses.
Consulting official public records: gazettes, land registries, public tenders and legal notices.
Searching people-search engines and online directories for publicly listed personal information.
Consulting public court records and case databases.
Searching public patent and trademark databases for filings and technical disclosures.
Analysing satellite or aerial imagery, including capture-date-aware comparison of imagery archives (e.g. Esri Wayback).
Tracking aircraft in near real time via ADS-B aggregators (e.g. Flightradar24, ADS-B Exchange).
Tracking ships via AIS aggregators (e.g. MarineTraffic, VesselFinder).
Pivoting on online maps and street-level imagery (e.g. Street View, Mapillary, KartaView) to geolocate and verify a scene.
Searching leaked or breached datasets for exposed emails, usernames or credentials (e.g. HaveIBeenPwned).
Analysing data dumps published on forums, paste sites or leak sites.
